name: Mike Beltran

items.why: Editing campaign website wording after a primary is a petty political moment, with no finding of wrongdoing and no bearing on any criterion, and the Washington Examiner reported no campaign explanation.

The matter is an opposing PAC's text-message attack about campaign donations, which is not proof of anything, and Beltran's cease-and-desist letter is his ordinary legal response, so it shows no conduct by him under the big-money criterion.

for_review: The Washington Examiner page was paywalled after the first two paragraphs. I could only read the lede, which says he removed prominent Trump mentions after winning the primary. I couldn't open the FL Voice article at all (fetch failed twice) and relied on the search-result excerpt for the Oct. 29 cease-and-desist letter. A person should read the full article and check Beltran's actual donor list against the PAC's text, which says he takes campaign cash from health insurance, tech and Wall Street companies. I didn't verify that claim. The owner-sites search (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) found nothing about Beltran. The results also showed that Castor was projected to beat Beltran in the FL-14 general election. Beltran has a history of suing over attack mailers, including a 2018 defamation suit and an August 2026 restraining order that a judge later dissolved. These look like ordinary campaign litigation rather than misconduct.
